key_insight: A large language model pipeline can extract both cannabis use status and reasons for use from unstructured EHR notes, with fine-tuned GatorTron best for status classification and an LLM best for reason identification.
clinical_relevance: This approach could enable better real-world studies of symptom self-management and cannabis-related outcomes in autoimmune rheumatic disease populations.
method: Screened EHR notes with fuzzy keyword matching and 50-word context windows.
Annotated 886 snippets for cannabis use status and 1,027 snippets for reasons for use.
Compared zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned LLMs, including GatorTron 345M, on held-out validation data.
evidence_signal: The study used retrospective ARD notes from 2015–2024 and evaluated models with accuracy, F1, recall, and precision on annotated validation sets.
watch_item: Performance may depend on note quality, keyword coverage, and local documentation patterns, so external validation is needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: Extracting patient reported cannabis use and reasons for use from electronic health records: a benchmarking study of large language models
